findings.desc: Automatic causal-successor post-pass allowed model-authored content to silence a blocking STOP.
Automatic continuation rule was fail-open for v1 predecessors during staged adoption.
A historical-noop successor could be treated as proof that an earlier STOP was disposed.
Continuation evidence was collected before target and callback binding checks.
The proposed automatic STOP resolution contradicted the unchanged fail-closed STOP contract.
The first patch lacked a regression proving STOP remains blocking and recovery terminates idempotently.
Automatic resolved-STOP evidence was not surfaced in tick output.
The operator guide would become stale if STOP were automatically hidden as idle.
